title: Single Number III
spaceBreakdown:
- long long xor2, mask: O(1) scalars
- int a, b: O(1) scalars
- returned vector<int>: 2 elements, not counted (LeetCode convention)
- no containers, no recursion
approach: XOR all numbers together: duplicate pairs cancel (x ⊕ x = 0), leaving `xor2 = a ⊕ b`. Since a ≠ b, `xor2` is nonzero and has at least one set bit where a and b differ. Isolate the lowest such bit with `mask = xor2 & -xor2` (computed in `long long` to avoid overflow when `xor2 = INT_MIN`). Partition the array by that bit and XOR each group separately - each group contains one unique plus cancelling pairs, yielding a and b.
hints: Every element except two appears exactly twice. What property of those pairs could let you eliminate all of them in a single combining pass over the array?

XOR all elements → `a ⊕ b`. Use the lowest set bit of that result to split the array into two groups; XOR each group separately to recover a and b. For [1,2,1,3,2,5]: XOR all → 6 (= 3 ⊕ 5), lowest set bit = 2, split by bit 2 → groups XOR to 3 and 5.

```
xor2 = XOR of all elements
mask = xor2 & (-xor2)        // lowest set bit
a = 0, b = 0
for each x in array:
    if x & mask:  a = a XOR x
    else:         b = b XOR x
return [a, b]
```

**Wrong mask bit** - xor2 may have bit 0 unset, so a fixed bit position fails.
`Input: nums = [1,2,1,3,2,5]` → `Expected: [3,5]`
⚠️ Bug: hardcoding `mask = 1` instead of extracting a set bit from xor2 → xor2 = 6 (110₂) has bit 0 unset, so 3 (011₂) and 5 (101₂) both have bit 0 set and land in the same group → returns [6, 0]

**Negative numbers** - sign extension must be preserved when testing the mask bit.
`Input: nums = [-1,0]` → `Expected: [-1,0]`
⚠️ Bug: guarding the XOR with `if (x > 0)` → both -1 and 0 are skipped → returns [0, 0]

**Operator precedence** - `&` binds looser than `!=` in C++.
`Input: nums = [2,2,4,6]` → `Expected: [4,6]`
⚠️ Bug: writing `if (x & mask != 0)` parses as `if (x & (mask != 0))` = `if (x & 1)` → all elements are even so all go to group b → returns [0, 2]

**INT_MIN overflow** - negating INT_MIN in `int` is undefined behaviour.
`Input: nums = [-2147483648,0]` → `Expected: [-2147483648,0]`
⚠️ Bug: `int mask = xor2 & -xor2` when xor2 = -2147483648 → -(-2147483648) = 2147483648 overflows 32-bit int → compiler exploiting UB may eliminate the mask → returns [0, 0]

followUps.q: What if exactly one element appears once instead of two?
followUps.a: XOR all elements - duplicates cancel, leaving the single value. Same bit-manipulation principle, no partitioning needed. O(n) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if exactly three elements appear once and all others twice?
followUps.a: XOR all to get a⊕b⊕c. For each of the 32 bit positions, count how many array elements have that bit set; if the count is odd, an odd number of the three uniques share that bit. This gives enough equations to reconstruct a, b, c individually. O(32n) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if the data arrives as a stream you can read only once?
followUps.a: Replace the second pass with 32 running XOR accumulators - accumulator i holds the XOR of all elements whose i-th bit is set. After the stream ends, combine these with the total XOR to recover a and b. O(32n) time, O(1) space.
